Its head is a tall faceted crystal shape like a long rough-cut gemstone growing out of the top of the soft neck; its front is one large blank polished facet, gently curved and uneven like natural crystal, with glowing colour moving deep inside. The milky flesh and pink sinew of the neck climb up over the lower edges of the crystal and between its lower facets, so there is no rim or seam, and small crystals continue in rows down the back of the neck. It wears a layered robe of crystal plates and silver mirror-thread fabric, open at the throat. This is Tamsa of the Clear Aperture, a Glasswright wing-mistress: a flock of tiny glass craft like starlings swirls round her raised hand of long tapering fingers, a wide collar shaped like an opening aperture ring. Painted grimdark science-fiction character portrait, oil painting with visible loose brushstrokes and palette-knife texture, dramatic chiaroscuro, square composition.
